text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Local government byelections will be held in 11 of Nigeria's states on Thursday. The byelections come after boundary changes in some constituencies and inconclusive results of March elections in others.
- Nigeria's second city of Ibadan, in the southwest, says it needs 2.4 billion naira to combat soil erosion which has led to flooding.

- Institute of Marine Engineers advises government to return the headquarters of the Nigerian Ports Authority to the port city and commercial capital of Lagos. Last year the headquarters was moved to the landlocked new administrative capital Abuja.
- Team from Aviation Development Company (ADC) airline leaves for eastern city of Calabar to investigate the cause of an aircraft accident on Tuesday.
- Lagos State government acquires asphalt plant for use in road repairs. The plant is estimated to have cost 200 million naira and is capable of producing 7,200 tonnes of asphalt per day.

- President of Nigerian Stock Exchange Goodie Ibru warns against a possible new exchange, which would be established in Abuja. Ibru said that he saw no need for the second exchange and that setting it up would send the wrong signal to investors.
